1Purpose

This policy sets out what [Provider name] commits to when a participant needs behaviour support urgently, before a full assessment is possible. It is for participants, their families and advocates, the providers who support them, our and the people who check our work.

2Applies to

  • Every participant we are asked to help, or find, who has an for behaviour support. This includes a participant whose providers are using, or are likely to use, a that no behaviour support plan covers.
  • Every Practitioner, , manager and worker of [Provider name], contractors included, who takes part in an interim plan.
  • Every setting: the participant's own home, a shared home, a day service, a school, a hospital or the community.
  • Specialist behaviour support only. A provider that only implements plans uses POL-BSP-08 Interim Behaviour Support Plans Policy (Implementing Behaviour Support Plans).

3Commitments

C1

We will decide the urgency of every referral within 1 , using the bands in PRO-SBS-06. A referral that is not an immediate need goes to the right pathway the same day, and we tell the referrer why.

C2

We will answer in writing every referral that needs an interim plan. For danger now we answer the same business day, and for urgent within 2 business days. If we cannot take it, we say so in that time and help the referrer find another specialist behaviour support provider.

Answers: Legislation, indicator (1)Legislation (1)How we do it: PRO-SBS-06, step 5PRO-SBS-06 step 5PRO-SBS-06, step 6PRO-SBS-06 step 6PRO-SBS-06, step 7PRO-SBS-06 step 7

C3

We will put safety first. Where anyone is in danger now, we tell the referrer to call 000 before we ask anything else. We check what keeps people safe until the plan is . We do this on the day we accept for danger now, and within 1 business day for urgent.

Answers: Legislation, indicator (1)Legislation (1)How we do it: PRO-SBS-06, step 1PRO-SBS-06 step 1PRO-SBS-06, step 9PRO-SBS-06 step 9

C4

We will use only a Practitioner, an NDIS behaviour support practitioner whom the Commissioner considers suitable, to evaluate the risk and write the plan. That includes any contractor we engage. A Clinical Supervisor checks every interim plan before it is issued.

Answers: Legislation, indicator (1)Legislation (1)How we do it: PRO-SBS-06, step 5PRO-SBS-06 step 5PRO-SBS-06, step 26PRO-SBS-06 step 26

C5

We will record an on the day we accept a referral. We will issue the interim plan within 5 business days of it for danger now, and within 10 for urgent. Where a regulated restrictive practice is involved, we will never issue it later than 1 month after the engagement date. We will issue the comprehensive plan within 6 months of it; 84 days is our target. An interim plan's review date is the comprehensive plan's due date, never 12 months. The Service Manager checks every open plan against these dates at least every week.

We will involve the participant in evaluating the risk, in the way they choose. We show them the draft plan before it is final. We give them their copy in a form they can use, and we explain it. We do this within 1 business day of issuing the plan, and before we tell anyone else.

C7

We will involve every provider that carries out the participant's supports in evaluating the risk and in considering the draft plan. We also take account of earlier assessments, and of what family, carers and other services tell us, with the participant's consent.

Answers: Legislation, indicator (1)Legislation (1)How we do it: PRO-SBS-06, step 11PRO-SBS-06 step 11PRO-SBS-06, step 13PRO-SBS-06 step 13PRO-SBS-06, step 14PRO-SBS-06 step 14PRO-SBS-06, step 25PRO-SBS-06 step 25and 1 more

C8

We will evaluate the risk the behaviour poses to the participant and to others, and what may be driving it, before we write any strategy. We rate each risk and record it.

Answers: Legislation, indicator (1)Legislation (1)How we do it: PRO-SBS-06, step 12PRO-SBS-06 step 12PRO-SBS-06, step 13PRO-SBS-06 step 13PRO-SBS-06, step 15PRO-SBS-06 step 15PRO-SBS-06, step 16PRO-SBS-06 step 16PRO-SBS-06, step 17PRO-SBS-06 step 17and 2 more

C9

We will write each interim plan on the Commissioner's approved form, or on another form that section 23(1) of allows and that holds every required item. Its content follows the Commission's Interim Behaviour Support Plan Checklist (October 2025): it is brief and usable; it evaluates the risk of harm; it does not include a functional behaviour assessment; it sets out changes within the environment; for any restrictive practice it says what is used, when, why, how and by whom; and it says how advice, and support will be given. Its strategies are evidence-based, person-centred and proactive. They address the participant's needs and the likely reason for the behaviour, and give the participant chances to build skills and join in community life.

C10

We will include a regulated restrictive practice in an interim plan only if it is authorised, or is on the state or territory's interim or short term pathway, and the plan identifies it clearly and states its authorisation status. Where authorisation is not yet in place, the plan says the practice must not be used, and says what happens until authorisation is granted. The plan also says how the practice will be reduced and ended. It must also meet every test in the Rules: last resort, least restrictive, in proportion to the risk and for the shortest time. We never include a practice that the state or territory prohibits.

We check that they can follow it. Only with the participant's consent, we give the same guidance to their in the same time.

4Ground rules

G1

This policy and every interim plan authorise no regulated restrictive practice. Only the authorisation process of the state or territory can do that, where it has one.

G2

Safety comes before paperwork. Nobody holds back a safety step while a service agreement or funding is sorted out. We complete AGR-SUP-01 Service Agreement Template alongside the work. If the participant's NDIS plan has no behaviour support funding, the Chief Executive decides whether we start the interim plan, and records the decision.

G3

An interim plan never waits for the full assessment. The functional behaviour assessment belongs to the comprehensive plan, under PRO-BSP-03 Functional Behaviour Assessments and Behaviour Support Plans Procedure.

G4

The engagement date is the date we agree in writing to develop the plan, or the date a regulated restrictive practice was first used and led to the referral, whichever is earlier (our standard). The Commission treats a provider as engaged from the service agreement date, or a later start date the agreement names, so our date is never later than the Commission's. Our written acceptance states that it is the start date for developing the plan for the purposes of the Rules, section 19, and the service agreement (AGR-SUP-01 Service Agreement Template) records the same date. We do not wait for a signed service agreement. PRO-BSP-03 sets the general rule.

G5

Where a regulated restrictive practice is in use or likely, we apply the 1 month and 6 month limits in section 19 of the Rules. The Rules set them where a practice has been used and we are engaged as a result. We apply them to a likely practice too. This is our standard.

G6

Nobody at [Provider name] can extend a time limit that the law sets. A late step is recorded with its reason. The dates on the register are never changed to hide it.

G7

Only a Practitioner evaluates the risk and writes the plan. Other workers, families and providers give information, records and views. No automated tool decides a risk or writes a plan on its own. A tool that helps with a draft gets only information with names and details removed. The Practitioner answers for every word (POL-TEC-01 Artificial Intelligence and Automated Tools Policy).

G8

We presume every participant can decide, with support (POL-RGT-03 Independence and Informed Choice Policy). Where another person holds legal authority, we see the order or instrument and record what it covers. We share a participant's information only as they consent, or as the law requires or allows. If consent is refused, we explain what that means, offer an independent advocate and tell the Clinical Supervisor the same day. The Practitioner goes on with the collection and consultation that the Rules require for a plan containing a restrictive practice (the Rules, section 20(3); Privacy Act 1988, Australian Privacy Principles 3 and 6, where collection or use is required or authorised by law), collects only what the plan needs, and records the refusal and what was collected despite it. The safety steps with the provider go on. The wording of this ground rule is settled once by legal advice on the template, not decided case by case.

G9

A regulated restrictive practice used without authorisation, or outside the plan, can be a reportable incident for the provider that used it. See , section 16. We support that provider under POL-SBS-06 Reportable Incidents Involving the Use of a Restrictive Practice Policy (Specialist Behaviour Support).

G10

In a sole practitioner business, the Practitioner holds the Service Manager, , Quality Manager and Chief Executive roles and does what those roles do, with two exceptions. The external Clinical Supervisor, engaged in writing and named in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register, does the Service Manager's checks on the Practitioner's own work, and makes any reportable-incident decision with the Practitioner. REG-GOV-01 also names a cover Practitioner, who must be an NDIS behaviour support practitioner and is arranged in writing before they are needed, and an independent contact for concerns, who reads REG-SBS-01 every 3 months.

G11

A concern about a colleague or a manager goes to the Clinical Supervisor. A concern about the Clinical Supervisor goes to the Clinical Lead. A concern about the Service Manager or the Clinical Lead goes to the Chief Executive. A concern about the Chief Executive goes to the chair of the governing body. Where one person owns the provider, it goes to the independent contact for concerns (POL-INC-01 Incident Management Policy, Ground rules). Nobody is punished for raising it.

G12

A participant, family member, carer or advocate can complain about an interim plan, or about how we made it. We handle it under POL-FBK-01 Feedback and Complaints Management Policy. A complaint never delays a safety step.

436 words
the Rules
the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Restrictive Practices and Behaviour Support) Rules 2018.
the Incident Rules
the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Incident Management and Reportable Incidents) Rules 2018.
interim behaviour support plan
a plan written quickly to manage the risk of a participant's behaviour until a comprehensive plan replaces it.
immediate need
the participant's behaviour puts them or others at risk of harm now or soon, and no plan manages it. It also covers a regulated restrictive practice in use, or likely to be used, that no plan covers.
urgency band
the group a referral is placed in: danger now, urgent, not immediate, or covered by a current plan. PRO-SBS-06 sets them.
comprehensive behaviour support plan
the full plan that follows a behaviour support assessment and a functional behaviour assessment.
Practitioner
an NDIS behaviour support practitioner. The Commissioner considers this person suitable to do behaviour support assessments and write plans that may include restrictive practices.
Clinical Supervisor
an experienced Practitioner who checks the Practitioner's work and supports their practice.
Clinical Lead
the senior Practitioner who owns clinical practice at [Provider name].
implementing provider
a provider whose workers carry out the participant's supports and will carry out the plan.
support network
the family, carers, friends, advocates and others the participant chooses.
regulated restrictive practice
seclusion, chemical restraint, mechanical restraint, physical restraint or environmental restraint, as the Rules define them (the Rules, section 6). A locked cupboard is environmental. A bed rail used to stop movement is mechanical. A medicine given mainly to change behaviour is chemical.
authorisation
the permission a state or territory gives, through its own process, for a regulated restrictive practice. Some states and territories have no such process.
interim pathway
a state or territory's short term or interim authorisation route for a practice that must be used before full authorisation can be decided, where the state or territory has one.
engagement date
the date we agree in writing to develop the plan, or the date a regulated restrictive practice was first used and led to the referral, whichever is earlier. The clocks in the Rules, section 19, run from it.
lodge
send to the Commissioner, in the form and the way the Commissioner requires.
issued
finalised and in force, on the date the Practitioner signs the plan. Issued, finalised and in force mean the same date in this policy and in PRO-SBS-06.
guidance
teaching and coaching on how to carry out the plan, with a check that it was understood.
business day
a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where the participant lives.

docs.html:
1Purpose

The result: every participant we assess gets an assessment that finds their unmet needs and the function of their behaviour. They get a plan written with them and with the people who carry it out. Those providers accept it, and a plan with a reaches the Commissioner on time.

This procedure gives effect to POL-SBS-03 Functional Behaviour Assessments and Behaviour Support Plans Policy, C1 to C14.

"Behaviour Support Rules" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Restrictive Practices and Behaviour Support) Rules 2018.

2When and who

Start this procedure when:

  • we receive a referral for a behaviour support assessment or plan
  • we take over a participant from another specialist provider
  • a review under PRO-SBS-04 Behaviour Support Plan Monitoring and Review Procedure says a plan must change, or the assessment revisit date is within 30 days.

Only a specialist behaviour support provider uses this procedure. A provider that only carries out plans uses PRO-BSP-05 Supporting the Assessment and Development of Behaviour Support Plans Procedure.

Who acts:

  • The Service Manager logs the referral, sets the dates, allocates the people, prepares each lodgement and keeps the register.
  • The triages the risk.
  • The does every assessment, writes every plan and it in the Commission's portal.
  • The checks each report and each plan.
  • The Quality Manager and the Chief Executive check the register and receive anything late. The Quality Manager decides whether an incident is reportable and notifies the Commission.

In a small provider one person may hold several roles. A sole Practitioner holds the Service Manager, Quality Manager and Chief Executive roles, except that the decision whether an incident is reportable is made by the outside Clinical Supervisor with them. The Clinical Supervisor is always someone outside, is the Clinical Lead for this procedure, and does the Service Manager's checks on the sole Practitioner's own work. Where a step says to tell another role, a sole Practitioner writes it on the plan row and tells the Clinical Supervisor.

Terms in this procedure:

  • Practitioner: an NDIS behaviour support practitioner, a person the Commissioner considers suitable to assess behaviour and write plans (Behaviour Support Rules, section 5).
  • plan: a behaviour support plan, interim or comprehensive.
  • assessment report: the written record of the assessment, on FRM-SBS-03 Functional Behaviour Assessment Report Template.
  • cover sheet: the record of how a plan was checked, shared and lodged, on FRM-BSP-02 Behaviour Support Plan Cover Sheet and Lodgement Record.
  • plan row: one line of REG-SBS-01 Behaviour Support Plan Register for one plan version.
  • : a provider that carries out the strategies in a plan.
  • regulated restrictive practice: seclusion, chemical restraint, mechanical restraint, physical restraint or environmental restraint (Behaviour Support Rules, section 6).
  • : the date we agree in writing to develop the plan, or the date a regulated restrictive practice was first used, whichever is earlier (POL-SBS-03 ground rule 7). Where that use was before the referral reached us, the date the referral reached us. A later date named in a service agreement never moves it.
  • in force: a plan is in force from the date the Practitioner finalises and signs it.

3Before you start

  • You are a Practitioner the Commissioner considers suitable, or you are supporting one.
  • You can open REG-SBS-01 Behaviour Support Plan Register.
  • You have FRM-SBS-03 Functional Behaviour Assessment Report Template and FRM-BSP-02 Behaviour Support Plan Cover Sheet and Lodgement Record, on paper or in the system.
  • You have the participant's communication preferences: FRM-RGT-01 Communication, Advocacy and Support Preferences Form.
  • You know where FRM-INF-01 Consent to Collect, Use and Share Information Form is kept.
  • You know your Clinical Supervisor's name and how to reach them.
  • You know the state or territory where the participant lives. Its law decides who can consent and which practices need .

4Watch out

  • If anyone is in danger, call 000 first. Tell the Service Manager after. A delay can cost a life.
  • Only a suitable Practitioner may assess or write. Anyone else doing it breaks a condition of our registration (Behaviour Support Rules, sections 17 and 18).
  • No consent, no assessment. Gathering information without valid consent breaches the participant's privacy and their right to decide.
  • Look for pain and illness first. A plan built on the wrong cause leaves the participant in pain and does not work.
  • The clocks start at engagement. Where a regulated restrictive practice led to our engagement, missing the 1 month or the 6 month limit breaks a condition of registration (Behaviour Support Rules, section 19).
  • A restrictive practice never enters through the back door. One that reaches a plan without consultation, notice and authorisation can be used on the participant unlawfully.
  • Lodge whether or not the practice is authorised. ask for the plan either way (Behaviour Support Rules, section 24(2)).
  • A plan nobody accepted may not be followed. Workers who have not seen it may respond in unsafe or uneven ways.

5Steps

Take the referral

Step 1

Service Manager

Log the referral.

Write down the date, who referred the participant and why, in the referrer's words. Say if we are taking over from another specialist provider.

Result
The referral is on record with its date.
Record
FRM-SBS-03 Q1, Q2
Time limit
Same (our standard)
Step 2

Warning. A participant at immediate risk, or a regulated restrictive practice already in use, cannot wait for a full assessment. Delay leaves people unsafe and can break the 1 month limit.

Clinical Lead, or a Practitioner the Clinical Lead names

Triage the risk.

If anyone is in danger now, tell the referrer to call 000. Ask what has happened, whether a regulated restrictive practice has been used, who uses it, how often, and who is at risk. Choose the row in Decision table 1. If the row needs an interim plan, tell the Service Manager now and start PRO-SBS-06 Interim Behaviour Support Plans Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support). Do not wait for the assessment.

Result
We know whether this is urgent and which plan is needed first.
Record
FRM-SBS-03 Q4
Time limit
Within 1 business day of the referral (our standard)
Step 3

Service Manager

Confirm we can take the referral.

Check that the participant chose us and that our registration covers specialist behaviour support. Check that a suitable Practitioner is free, their NDIS plan funds behaviour support and a service agreement is signed (AGR-SUP-01 Service Agreement Template). Open the plan row in REG-SBS-01 and write the engagement date: the date we agree in writing to develop the plan, or the date a regulated restrictive practice was first used, whichever is earlier. Where that use was before the referral reached us, use the date the referral reached us. Starting assessment or plan work counts as agreeing to develop the plan. A later start date in the agreement never moves it.

Result
We have agreed to take the referral, the plan row is open and the engagement date is recorded.
Record
FRM-SBS-03 Q3; REG-SBS-01 col A
Time limit
Before any assessment work starts. The same day where risk is urgent (our standard)
Step 4

Service Manager

Work out the due dates.

Use Decision table 1, counting from the engagement date set at step 3 (the date we agree in writing to develop the plan, or the date a regulated restrictive practice was first used, whichever is earlier). Where a regulated restrictive practice was used and led to our engagement, the interim plan is due 1 month after the engagement date. The comprehensive plan is due 6 months after it. In every other case the comprehensive plan is due 84 days after it. The assessment report is always due 49 days after it. Put each date in the diary of the Practitioner and the Service Manager.

Result
Every due date is on the plan row and in two diaries.
Record
FRM-SBS-03 Q5
Time limit
Same day as step 3 (our standard)
Step 5

Warning. An assessment or plan written by a person the Commissioner has not found suitable breaks a condition of our registration.

Service Manager

Allocate a Practitioner and a Clinical Supervisor.

Confirm the Practitioner's suitability under PRO-SBS-01 Behaviour Support in the NDIS Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support). Check a contractor the same way. Do not allocate anyone who is still waiting for the Commissioner's decision. Name the Clinical Supervisor. A sole Practitioner names an outside Clinical Supervisor.

Result
A suitable Practitioner and a Clinical Supervisor are named on the plan row.
Record
FRM-SBS-03 Q6, Q7
Time limit
Within 2 business days of step 3 (our standard)

Get consent

Step 6

Warning. A family member, carer or provider cannot consent for an adult unless they hold legal authority. Collecting or sharing information without valid consent breaches the participant's privacy and their right to decide.

Practitioner

Ask the participant for consent.

Meet the participant in the way that suits them. Use their communication preferences. Explain what the assessment is, what we will collect, from whom, who will see it, and that they can stop at any time. Use Decision table 2 to find who decides. Offer an independent advocate. Ask for consent to assess, to ask named people and services for information, and to share the report. Record each answer, including each no, on FRM-INF-01 Consent to Collect, Use and Share Information Form.

Result
The participant has decided in their own way, and we know who we may ask and who we may tell.
Record
FRM-SBS-03 Q9 to Q14
Time limit
Before you collect any information. First meeting within 10 business days of the engagement date (our standard)

Assess

Step 7

Warning. A behaviour can be the only way a participant can say they are in pain or unwell. A plan built on the wrong cause leaves the participant in pain and will not work.

Practitioner

Ask for a health review.

With consent, ask the participant's doctor or another health practitioner to review pain, illness, medicines and their side effects, sleep, hearing, vision, sensory needs and mental health. Do not diagnose. Do not advise a change of medicine. Only the prescriber decides that. If the review cannot happen quickly, record what you asked, of whom and when.

Result
A health practitioner has looked for health causes, or a dated request is on record with a date to chase it.
Record
FRM-SBS-03 Q24
Time limit
Ask within 5 business days of consent (our standard)
Step 8

Practitioner

Ask for what is already known.

With consent, ask for earlier assessments and plans, allied health and medical reports, school or day service records, and assessments by other providers and mainstream services. Ask each implementing provider for its incident reports and behaviour records (FRM-BSP-04 Behaviour Record). If we are taking over from another specialist provider, ask for the current plan, its lodgement and authorisation details and its data. Our own clocks still run from our engagement date. Record what you asked for and what arrived.

Result
Every source is listed with its date, and each gap is written down.
Record
FRM-SBS-03 Q16, Q18 to Q20
Time limit
Within 10 business days of consent (our standard)
Step 9

Practitioner

Collect direct and indirect data.

Watch the participant yourself in each setting where the behaviour happens, at the times it happens. Interview the participant, their and workers. Use behaviour charts and rating tools. Record the period and the settings, and say why they are long enough. Workers and family supply records. They do not assess.

Result
The assessment rests on what you saw and what people told you, from every setting.
Record
FRM-SBS-03 Q15, Q17
Time limit
Finish before the assessment report is due, 49 days after the engagement date (our standard)
Step 10

Practitioner

Ask the participant what matters to them.

Ask in their way and in their words. Cover their strengths, likes and goals, what is going well and what is not, culture and language, how they communicate, their history, and what home and routines are like. Ask only about history they choose to share. If the participant is Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander, ask who in their community they want to advise us.

Result
The assessment is about the whole person, their own words are in it and their unmet needs are known.
Record
FRM-SBS-03 Q21 to Q23, Q25 to Q28
Time limit
Within 10 business days of consent (our standard)
Step 11

Practitioner

Describe each behaviour of concern.

Write what an observer can see and hear, not what you think it means. Record how often, how long and how intense it is, using a scale you name. Record early warning signs, how it ends, who is at risk and how seriously. Rate the risk of harm.

Result
Anyone can recognise and count each behaviour, and the risk is rated.
Record
FRM-SBS-03 Q29 to Q32
Time limit
Before the assessment report is due (our standard)
Step 12

Practitioner

Work out the function of each behaviour.

Look at setting events, triggers and what follows the behaviour. Write one summary statement for each behaviour. Say what evidence supports it and what would show it wrong. Say which other explanations you ruled out. Name a skill or behaviour that could meet the same need.

Result
Each behaviour has a testable function and a replacement skill.
Record
FRM-SBS-03 Q33 to Q38
Time limit
Before the assessment report is due (our standard)
Step 13

Practitioner

Map the participant's other supports and services.

List every NDIS and other support the participant uses: health, mental health, education, housing, justice, day and community services. Record what each does, who to contact and what it does when the behaviour happens. Say how they should fit together and what protocol each needs. With the participant's consent, ask each service to agree.

Result
We know every service and what each must do for the plan to work across them.
Record
FRM-SBS-03 Q44, Q45
Time limit
Before the assessment report is due (our standard)
Step 14

Warning. Apart from a single emergency use, a regulated restrictive practice used without authorisation breaks a condition of registration for the provider using it (Behaviour Support Rules, s 9(2)(a)). It can also harm the participant.

Practitioner

List every restrictive practice now in use.

Include any practice, regulated or not, and any practice in an earlier plan. Record who uses it, where, how often and since when. Record whether it is authorised and whether it is in a current plan. If you see a practice that could cause serious harm, such as a restraint that restricts breathing: call 000 if anyone is in danger, tell the person to stop, and tell the Service Manager the same day. If a regulated restrictive practice is in use without authorisation, tell the implementing provider in writing the same day. Then start PRO-SBS-05 Reportable Incidents Involving the Use of a Restrictive Practice Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support); the implementing provider notifies the Commission of its own use, and the Quality Manager decides whether it is also reportable by us. If you think a regulated restrictive practice may be needed in the plan (FRM-SBS-03 Q43), tell the Service Manager and start PRO-SBS-02 Restrictive Practices Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support) now, before the plan is drafted. Do not recommend a restrictive practice in the report.

Result
Every practice in use is on record with its status, and this report adds none.
Record
FRM-SBS-03 Q39 to Q43
Time limit
Same day for a practice that could cause serious harm. Otherwise before the assessment report is due (our standard)
Step 15

Practitioner

Write the assessment report.

Finish the recommendations in this order: changes to the environment; skills and replacement behaviours; proactive strategies; response strategies. Add the data each implementing provider should collect, the training they need, and chances for the participant to join community activities and learn new skills. Say whether an automated tool was used. Give the report its number. Set the date to revisit it.

Result
The report is complete and ready for checking.
Record
FRM-SBS-03 Q8, Q46 to Q53, Q56, Q57
Time limit
Within 49 days of the engagement date (our standard)
Step 16

Clinical Supervisor

Check the assessment report.

Check that consent is valid, a health cause was looked at, each function rests on evidence and the sources are listed. Check that no restrictive practice is recommended. Sign the sign-off block, or send the report back with the changes needed.

Result
The report is signed off, or returned with reasons.
Record
FRM-SBS-03 Q58
Time limit
Within 3 business days of receiving it (our standard)
Step 17

Practitioner

Go through the findings with the participant.

Use their way of communicating. Say what you found and what you recommend. Ask what they think. Write down any disagreement in their words. Share the findings with others only as the participant agreed.

Result
The participant has heard the findings and said what they think.
Record
FRM-SBS-03 Q54, Q55
Time limit
Within 5 business days of step 16 (our standard)

Write the plan

Step 18

Practitioner

Consult each implementing provider.

With the participant's consent, meet each provider that will carry out the plan. Ask what the plan can ask of them in their setting, who does what, what data they can collect and what training they need. Write down each answer. Consult while you write. Do not wait for the draft.

Result
Each implementing provider has been heard before the plan is drafted.
Record
FRM-BSP-02 Q11
Time limit
Before you finish the draft (our standard)
Step 19

Warning. A plan copied from another participant, or written on a template that misses an item the Commission's checklist requires, puts wrong strategies into practice and can break the Rules.

Practitioner

Draft the plan on a permitted, complete template.

Use the Commission's current template, our own approved template that holds every item in the Commission's plan checklist, or the template the state or territory authorising body requires (Behaviour Support Rules, section 23(1)). Check the Commission's website on the day you start for the current checklist and template edition. Write strategies from this participant's assessment report only. Cover every item in the plan content check (FRM-BSP-02 Q13). Give the participant chances to join community activities and learn new skills. Record each source you used. For each regulated restrictive practice, write the protocol the Commission's checklist requires. For a chemical restraint, copy the medication, dose, route and frequency exactly from the prescriber's current order and name the prescriber and the date of the order; you never decide or change a dose.

Result
A complete draft exists on a permitted template.
Record
FRM-BSP-02 Q1 to Q6
Time limit
Within 5 business days of step 16, alongside step 17 (our standard)
Step 20

Practitioner

If the draft includes, or may include, a regulated restrictive practice:

Check that the restrictive practice process is complete.

PRO-SBS-02 Restrictive Practices Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support) was started at step 14, when a practice first looked likely. Check now that the consultation, the notice of intention in a form the participant can understand, the risks, the alternatives and the state or territory authorisation route are all recorded. Do not finalise the plan until FRM-SBS-02 Restrictive Practice Consultation Record is complete and the Clinical Supervisor has decided at PRO-SBS-02 step 22.

Result
The practice has been consulted on, noticed and authorised, or it is taken out of the draft.
Record
FRM-BSP-02 Q7, Q8
Time limit
Before the plan is finalised (our standard, giving effect to Behaviour Support Rules, s 20(2) and s 20(4))
Step 21

Practitioner

Give the draft to the participant.

Give it in a form they understand, such as plain words, pictures or a spoken summary. Go through it with them. Offer an independent advocate. Ask what they want changed. Write down their view, and any disagreement in their words. Change the draft where the change keeps them safe. If they still disagree, tell the Clinical Supervisor.

Result
The participant has seen the draft and said what they think.
Record
FRM-BSP-02 Q9, Q10
Time limit
Within 1 business day of finishing the draft (our standard)
Step 22

Practitioner

Send the draft to each implementing provider.

With the participant's consent, send the draft for consideration and written acceptance. Ask for an answer within 5 business days. Ask each provider to say yes, yes with changes, or no, and why.

Result
Each implementing provider has the draft and a date to answer.
Record
FRM-BSP-02 Q11
Time limit
Within 1 business day of finishing the draft (our standard)
Step 23

Practitioner

Record each provider's answer.

Chase any provider that has not answered by business day 3. If a provider asks for a change that keeps the participant safe, change the draft and tell every provider what changed. If a provider declines, or has not answered by business day 5, see If it goes wrong.

Result
Every provider's answer, or its silence, is on record.
Record
FRM-BSP-02 Q12
Time limit
Chase at 3 business days. Close at 5 business days after sending (our standard)
Step 24

Clinical Supervisor

Check the final draft.

Check the draft against every item in the plan content check (FRM-BSP-02 Q13, built from the Commission's checklist). Check that each regulated restrictive practice is named, is authorised or going through authorisation, has a complete protocol, a reduction strategy and a review date, and passed Decision table 2 in PRO-SBS-02. Check that the template is permitted and complete. Sign it as cleared, or send it back with the changes needed.

Result
The plan is cleared for finalising, or returned with reasons.
Record
FRM-BSP-02 Q13, Q14
Time limit
Within 5 business days of receiving it, or 2 business days for an interim plan (our standard)
Step 25

Practitioner

Finalise and endorse the plan.

Sign and date the plan with your name, position, organisation, location and contact details. The date you sign is the date the plan is in force. Set the review date: for a comprehensive plan, no more than 12 months later; for an interim plan, the comprehensive plan's due date, never 12 months. Finalise only when the Clinical Supervisor has cleared the plan and the participant's view and each provider's answer are on record.

Result
The plan is in force from the date of signing.
Record
FRM-BSP-02 Q15
Time limit
Within 1 business day of the Clinical Supervisor's clearance at step 24 (our standard). Comprehensive plan: within 84 days of the engagement date (our standard; the step limits add up to about 77 days). Where a regulated restrictive practice was used and led to our engagement: within 6 months (statutory: Behaviour Support Rules, s 19(2)(b)). Interim plan in that case: within 1 month (statutory: s 19(2)(a))
Step 26

Practitioner

Give the plan to the participant and, with consent, to others.

Give the participant their plan in a form they understand, with the help they chose. With consent, give a copy to each person in the support network and each implementing provider. Tell each person to remove the old version. Record who got it, how and when.

Result
Everyone who should have the plan has the current version, and the participant knows what it says.
Record
FRM-BSP-02 Q16
Time limit
The participant: the same day as step 25. Each implementing provider: within 1 business day of step 25 (our standard)
Step 27

Warning. A plan that contains a regulated restrictive practice must reach the Commissioner whether or not the state or territory has authorised the practice. Lodging late, or not at all, breaks a condition of our registration.

Practitioner. The Service Manager prepares the lodgement

If the plan contains a regulated restrictive practice:

Lodge the plan with the Commissioner.

The Commission's portal requires the Practitioner to send the lodgement. The Service Manager may enter the data and prepare the draft; the Practitioner checks it and sends it. Attach what the Commission requires: the plan, the assessment report (FRM-SBS-03) for a comprehensive plan, each implementing provider's ABN and outlet, and the details of each practice (Behaviour Support Rules, section 23(1)(b)). Save the Commission's confirmation and write down its reference. Lodge each reviewed version in the same way. Tell each implementing provider the lodgement date. If lodgement fails, see If it goes wrong.

Result
The Commissioner has the plan and we hold the confirmation.
Record
FRM-BSP-02 Q17, Q18
Time limit
Within 5 business days of step 25 (our standard). The law says as soon as practicable (statutory: Behaviour Support Rules, s 24(1))
Step 28

Practitioner

Start the handover and training for implementing providers.

Follow PRO-SBS-03 Supporting the Implementation of the Behaviour Support Plan Procedure. Make a record on FRM-SBS-04 Behaviour Support Plan Handover and Training Record for each contact.

Result
Handover has started for each implementing provider.
Record
FRM-SBS-04; REG-SBS-01 col AL
Time limit
Within 5 business days of step 26, or 2 business days for an interim plan (our standard)

When a plan changes

Step 29

Practitioner

If a review under PRO-SBS-04 Behaviour Support Plan Monitoring and Review Procedure says the plan must change, or the participant's circumstances change, or the assessment revisit date is within 30 days:

Start a new version of the plan.

Check whether the function may have changed: a new setting, a health change, a loss, a new practice or new data. If it may have, revisit the assessment and update the report first. Each time, record that you looked. Then repeat steps 18 to 28 for the new version, and step 6 if consent has lapsed or the decision maker has changed. Lodge again if the plan contains a regulated restrictive practice.

Result
A new version exists, has passed every step, and the old version is ready to close.
Record
FRM-SBS-03 Q57; REG-SBS-01 col D
Time limit
Start within 5 business days of the trigger (our standard). For a plan with a regulated restrictive practice, the law says review as soon as practicable after a change that needs an amendment (statutory: Behaviour Support Rules, s 22(a))

Keep the record

Step 30

Service Manager

Update the plan row.

Copy each answer marked for REG-SBS-01 from FRM-SBS-03 and FRM-BSP-02. Update the status. Mark the old version superseded when its replacement is in force. Check the row against the Entry rules in REG-SBS-01. A correction is a new version of the row, with a reason.

Result
The plan row shows where the plan is up to, and every date can be traced to a form.
Record
FRM-BSP-02 Q19; REG-SBS-01 col BC; REG-SBS-01 col BE; REG-SBS-01 col BD
Time limit
Within 2 business days of each stage (our standard)

6Decision

Decision table 1: Which plan do we write, and by when?

Section 19 is not triggered by a takeover of a lodged plan that is in force (NDIS Commission position statement, February 2026; legal reviewer to confirm)
A review or an event means the plan must changeA new version. Revisit the assessment first if the function may have changed. Repeat the plan stepsStart within 5 business days (our standard). Lodge the new version within 5 business days of finalising it if it contains a regulated restrictive practice (our standard)

The step limits for a comprehensive plan add up to about 77 calendar days: the report by day 49, then the check (3 business days), the findings and the draft together (5 business days), sending (1 business day), the providers' answers (5 business days), the final check (5 business days) and finalising (1 business day). That sits inside the 84-day target with a week in hand. Where a regulated restrictive practice led to our engagement, the 6-month limit in section 19(2)(b) is the law and the 84 days is our target inside it.

Decision table 2: Who gives consent?

IfThen
The participant is a childA person with parental responsibility decides. Take the child's views into account and tell them what is happening in a way they understand. Ask to see any court order that changes who decides
The participant is a child in statutory careThe delegate of the Minister or agency that holds parental responsibility decides. Sight the delegation or order and record it. Take the child's views into account and tell them what is happening in a way they understand
The participant is a young person assessed as able to consent in their own rightThe law of [state or territory] decides whether a young person may consent to an assessment. Where it allows, the young person decides, with support; record the basis. Involve a person with parental responsibility as the young person agrees or as the law requires
The participant can decide with supportThe participant decides. Use their way of communicating, give them time and offer an independent advocate. Consult family and carers only if the participant agrees
A guardian or another decision maker has legal authority for this decisionThe decision maker decides, with the participant's views in front of them. Look at the document. Record the name, the source of the authority and the date you saw it. The authority covers only what the document says
A family member or carer says they speak for the participant but has no legal authorityThey cannot consent. Record what they say as the view of a member of the support network. Ask the participant. If the participant cannot decide and nobody has authority, stop and tell the Service Manager
The participant says no, or stops laterStop collecting information. Record what they said. See If it goes wrong
There is an urgent risk and consent cannot be obtained yetDo only the risk work in PRO-SBS-06. Do not start the assessment until consent is in place

The law of [state or territory] says who may consent for an adult and which practices need authorisation. Look it up before the first meeting.

7If it goes wrong

IfThen
The participant says no, or stopsStop collecting information and share nothing more. Record what they said. Offer an independent advocate and more time. Tell the Service Manager. Ask again after 10 business days, if they agree (our standard). If there is a risk of harm, keep the interim safety work in PRO-SBS-06 going without the assessment
Nobody has authority and the participant cannot decideStop. Tell the Service Manager the same day. The Service Manager asks the referrer and the participant's advocate who can decide, and records the answer. Do not accept a family member's word alone
The plan has no behaviour support funding, or no suitable Practitioner is freeThe Service Manager tells the participant and the referrer in writing the same day. The message says what they can do: ask their support coordinator or the NDIA to change the plan, or choose another provider. Do not start paid work. If the risk is urgent, tell the Chief Executive, who decides whether to start with an interim plan and records the decision
The Practitioner is absent or leavesThe Service Manager gives the work to another suitable Practitioner within 2 business days. The first Practitioner, or the Clinical Supervisor, hands over the file. Tell the participant and their support network. The due dates do not move
An implementing provider declines or does not answerRecord each attempt. Ask why, and offer a change that keeps the participant safe. After 2 attempts the Service Manager tells the participant, and decides with the Clinical Supervisor whether to finalise and how to keep the participant safe. Record the decision. A plan finalised without a provider's acceptance is marked "not accepted by [provider]" at FRM-BSP-02 Q12, and the notice to the Commissioner under PRO-SBS-04 Behaviour Support Plan Monitoring and Review Procedure starts the same day
A source will not give informationRecord your request and the reply. Carry on. List the gap in the assessment report. Never treat missing data as no behaviour
A due date will be missedTell the Service Manager as soon as you know, and at least 7 days before the date. The Service Manager tells the Chief Executive the same day, then the participant and each implementing provider. Record the reason, the new date and what keeps the participant safe in REG-SBS-01 col BB. The law lets nobody extend a limit it sets. For advice, phone the NDIS Commission on 1800 035 544. Never backdate a record
Lodgement failsTry again the same day. Save the error and the time. Phone the Commission. Record what happened in REG-SBS-01 col AP. If the due date has passed, tell the Chief Executive the same day
The plan is out of date or no longer fitsStart step 29 at once. Until the new version is in force, nobody uses a practice the plan does not contain. If a regulated restrictive practice is used outside the plan, follow PRO-SBS-05 Reportable Incidents Involving the Use of a Restrictive Practice Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support)
The participant disagrees with the planWrite their view in their words. Offer an independent advocate. Tell them they can complain under PRO-FBK-01 Feedback and Complaints Management Procedure. If the disagreement is about a restrictive practice, PRO-SBS-02 sets what happens next
You are worried about a colleague or a managerTell the Clinical Supervisor. If it is about the Clinical Supervisor, tell the Service Manager, who uses the substitute (PRO-SBS-01 Decision table 4). If it is about the Service Manager, tell the Chief Executive. If it is about the Chief Executive, or about a sole Practitioner's own work, tell the Clinical Supervisor or phone the NDIS Commission on 1800 035 544. If you think a participant has been abused, neglected or restrained unlawfully, follow PRO-INC-01 Incident Management Procedure and PRO-SGD-01 Violence, Abuse, Neglect, Exploitation and Discrimination Procedure the same day
The participant leaves us or changes providerFollow PRO-SUP-04 Transitions to or from a Provider Procedure. With consent, give the new provider the current plan and the assessment report. Mark the row ended. Never delete it
The Practitioner is no longer considered suitableStop all assessment and plan work at once and tell the Service Manager. The Service Manager gives the work to another suitable Practitioner within 2 business days. The Clinical Supervisor checks the work already done before anyone relies on it. The due dates do not move
The system is downUse paper copies of FRM-SBS-03 Functional Behaviour Assessment Report Template and FRM-BSP-02 Behaviour Support Plan Cover Sheet and Lodgement Record. The Service Manager enters them within 2 business days of the system coming back

8Done means

  • The assessment report is complete, signed off by the Clinical Supervisor and gone through with the participant.
  • The plan is finalised and in force, on a permitted template that holds every item in the Commission's checklist, with the Practitioner's endorsement.
  • Each implementing provider was consulted, was sent the draft and has an answer on record.
  • The participant has their plan in a form they understand.
  • A plan with a regulated restrictive practice has been through PRO-SBS-02 Restrictive Practices Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support) and lodged with the Commissioner, and the confirmation is filed.
  • Handover has started under PRO-SBS-03 Supporting the Implementation of the Behaviour Support Plan Procedure.
  • These records now exist:
    • the assessment report, FRM-SBS-03 Functional Behaviour Assessment Report Template
    • the cover sheet, FRM-BSP-02 Behaviour Support Plan Cover Sheet and Lodgement Record
    • the consent record, FRM-INF-01 Consent to Collect, Use and Share Information Form
    • the consultation record, FRM-SBS-02 Restrictive Practice Consultation Record, where a practice is involved
    • a complete row in REG-SBS-01 Behaviour Support Plan Register.

9Quick card

134 words
  • If anyone is in danger, call 000 first, and tell anyone using a practice that could cause serious harm to stop (step 14)
  • Only a Practitioner the Commissioner considers suitable assesses or writes (step 5)
  • No consent, no assessment: ask the participant first (step 6)
  • Ask for a health review before you decide what a behaviour means (step 7)
  • Work out every due date the day you set the engagement date (step 4)
  • A restrictive practice goes in a plan only through PRO-SBS-02 (step 20)
  • Send the draft to each implementing provider and wait for each answer (step 22)
  • Give the participant their plan in a form they understand, the day it is final (step 26)
  • The Practitioner lodges every plan with a regulated restrictive practice within 5 business days of finalising (step 27)

10Control

docs.html:
1Purpose

The result: a participant with an for behaviour support has the risk evaluated with them and with the providers who support them. An interim plan that manages the risk is then , lodged where the law requires, and explained to the people who will carry it out.

This procedure gives effect to POL-SBS-07 Interim Behaviour Support Plans Policy, C1 to C14.

the : a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where the participant lives.

2When and who

Start this procedure when [Provider name] is told that a participant may have an immediate need for behaviour support. The news can come from an , a family member, the participant, a support coordinator, a plan manager, a hospital or the NDIS Commission. It can also come from our own . A provider may use FRM-BSP-08 Interim Behaviour Support Engagement Record to ask us.

Only a specialist behaviour support provider uses this procedure. A provider that only implements plans uses PRO-BSP-09 Interim Behaviour Support Plans Procedure (Implementing Behaviour Support Plans).

If PRO-BSP-03 has already logged and triaged the referral, use that record. Do not enter it again. Start at step 3, and set the target date at step 7.

Who acts:

  • Whoever takes the referral writes it down and tells the Service Manager.
  • The sets the .
  • The Service Manager answers the referral, sets the dates, the plan and keeps the clocks.
  • The Practitioner does the clinical work, from the first safety check to the close of the plan.
  • The checks the plan before it is issued.
  • The cover Practitioner takes over when the Practitioner is absent.
  • The Chief Executive is told when a legal limit will be missed.

A sole Practitioner holds the Service Manager, Clinical Lead, Quality Manager and Chief Executive roles and does what those roles do, with two exceptions. The external Clinical Supervisor named in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register does the Service Manager's checks on the Practitioner's own work, and makes any reportable-incident decision with the Practitioner. Where a step says to tell another role, a sole Practitioner writes it on the plan row and tells the Clinical Supervisor.

In this procedure:

  • "" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Restrictive Practices and Behaviour Support) Rules 2018
  • "" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Incident Management and Reportable Incidents) Rules 2018
  • "the Practice Standards Rules" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Provider Registration and Practice Standards) Rules 2018
  • "the plan row" means the line of REG-SBS-01 Behaviour Support Plan Register for this plan.

3Before you start

  • You know the referral number: [referral phone number]. Its message tells callers to ring 000 first if anyone is in danger now.
  • You can open REG-SBS-01 Behaviour Support Plan Register, FRM-SBS-03 Functional Behaviour Assessment Report Template and FRM-SBS-07 Interim Behaviour Support Risk Evaluation. You know where the paper copies are kept.
  • You know who the Practitioner, the Clinical Supervisor and the cover Practitioner are. You have the suitability record kept under PRO-SBS-01 Behaviour Support in the NDIS Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support).
  • You can find the schedule for the participant's state or territory in REG-QMS-03 Compliance Obligations Register.
  • You can get the Commissioner's current approved plan form through FRM-BSP-02 Behaviour Support Plan Cover Sheet and Lodgement Record.

4Watch out

  • Call 000 first. If anyone is in danger now, the referrer calls 000 before anything else. Our phone line cannot keep a person safe, and every question asked first costs time.
  • Do not advise a restrictive practice by phone. Advice to use one, with no plan and no authorisation, can make the provider's use unauthorised. The provider may then have to report it as a reportable incident.
  • The clock starts at engagement, not at the plan. The 1 month limit runs from the . Missing it breaches a condition of our registration (Rules, s 19(2)(a)). That can lead to a civil penalty (NDIS Act 2013, s 73J).
  • The other provider's clock may end sooner. Its 1 month limit runs from the first use of the practice. Step 8 tells it the date. The law is in the Rules, s 11(2), s 12(2) and s 13(2).
  • An interim plan does not wait for the full assessment. The functional behaviour assessment belongs to the comprehensive plan (Rules, s 20(5)). Holding the interim plan back for it leaves the risk unmanaged.
  • Never write an unauthorised practice as allowed. A worker who reads "allowed" will use it. The provider then uses a practice with no authority.
  • Sharing without consent breaches privacy. It can also put the participant at risk, for example if a family member is part of the concern.

5Steps

Take the referral

Step 1

Warning. Our phone line is not an emergency service. Time spent on questions first can cost a life.

Whoever takes the referral

If anyone is in danger now, or serious harm is about to happen:

Tell the referrer to call 000 first.

Say it before you ask any other question. If the referrer cannot call, call 000 yourself and give the address. Do not give advice on how to hold or confine the participant.

Result
Emergency help is on its way before we do anything else.
Record
FRM-SBS-07 Q3
Time limit
Straight away (our standard)

Carries out: Policy, commitment 3Policy C3Written on: FRM-SBS-07, question 3FRM-SBS-07 Q3

Step 2

Whoever takes the referral

Write down the referral in the referrer's own words.

Open FRM-SBS-03 and answer only its referral questions, Q1 to Q14, which serve as the intake record. The clinical sections wait for the Practitioner. Record who referred, when and how. Record who the participant is, where they are and who is at risk. Record what happened and what is being done now. Record whether anyone has used a restrictive practice, and the date it was first used. Say if we would be taking over from another specialist provider. Ask whether the participant knows about the referral. Tell the Service Manager. Use the paper copy of FRM-SBS-03 and FRM-SBS-07 if the system is down.

Result
The Service Manager has the whole referral, and nothing depends on memory.
Record
FRM-SBS-07 Q1 and Q4; FRM-SBS-03 Q1, Q2 and Q4; REG-SBS-01 (participant; referral received; engaged because of a )
Time limit
Within 1 hour of the referral (our standard)

Carries out: Policy, commitment 1Policy C1Written on: FRM-SBS-07, question 1FRM-SBS-07 Q1FRM-SBS-07, question 4FRM-SBS-07 Q4FRM-SBS-03, question 1FRM-SBS-03 Q1FRM-SBS-03, question 2FRM-SBS-03 Q2FRM-SBS-03, question 4FRM-SBS-03 Q4and 2 more

Step 3

Clinical Lead, or a Practitioner the Clinical Lead names

Set the urgency band using Decision table 1.

If you are unsure between two bands, choose the more urgent one. Ask the Clinical Supervisor if you cannot decide. Do not wait for more information before you decide.

Result
Every referral has a band and a reason, so the times that follow are fixed.
Record
FRM-SBS-07 Q2
Time limit
Within 1 business day of the referral, and straight away if step 1 applied (our standard)

Carries out: Policy, commitment 1Policy C1Written on: FRM-SBS-07, question 2FRM-SBS-07 Q2

Step 4

Service Manager

If the band is "Not immediate" or "Covered by a current plan":

Tell the referrer in writing where the referral goes and why.

Send the referral to PRO-BSP-03 Functional Behaviour Assessments and Behaviour Support Plans Procedure. It sets the assessment, the plan and the steps for taking over from another provider. For a plan we hold, send it to PRO-SBS-04 Behaviour Support Plan Monitoring and Review Procedure for an early review. Say why this is not an interim plan. Tell the referrer to call again straight away if anyone is in danger or things get worse.

Result
The referral is on the right pathway, and the referrer knows what to do if things get worse.
Record
FRM-SBS-07 Q6
Time limit
The same business day as step 3 (our standard)

Carries out: Policy, commitment 1Policy C1Written on: FRM-SBS-07, question 6FRM-SBS-07 Q6

Step 5

Service Manager

Decide whether we can take the referral.

Check three things. A suitable Practitioner can start within the times for the band. A Clinical Supervisor can check the plan before it is issued. Nobody involved has a conflict of interest (POL-GOV-02 Conflict of Interest Policy). Name the Practitioner and the Clinical Supervisor. Check the Practitioner's suitability on the record kept under PRO-SBS-01 Behaviour Support in the NDIS Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support); the Commission's outcome is suitable, not suitable or unable to decide, and it records no capability level. Do not wait for a signed service agreement. If the participant's NDIS plan has no behaviour support funding, tell the Chief Executive the same day. They decide whether to start the interim plan, and record the decision.

Result
We accept only a referral we can meet in time, with named people.
Record
FRM-SBS-03 Q6 and Q7; REG-SBS-01 (Practitioner; Clinical Supervisor)
Time limit
The same business day as the referral for danger now, and within 2 business days of the referral for urgent (our standard)

Carries out: Policy, commitment 2Policy C2Policy, commitment 4Policy C4Written on: FRM-SBS-03, question 6FRM-SBS-03 Q6FRM-SBS-03, question 7FRM-SBS-03 Q7

Step 6

Service Manager

If we cannot take the referral:

Tell the referrer in writing that we cannot take it.

Give the reason and the date. Give the names of other specialist behaviour support providers you know of. Ask the participant's support coordinator or plan manager, if there is one, to help. Where a restrictive practice has been used and is likely to continue, remind the referrer of the provider's own duty. It must take all reasonable steps to have an interim plan made within 1 month of the first use. A comprehensive plan is due within 6 months (Rules, s 11(2), s 12(2) and s 13(2)).

Result
The referrer can act the same day with another provider.
Record
FRM-SBS-07 Q6
Time limit
The same business day as the decision at step 5 (our standard)

Carries out: Policy, commitment 2Policy C2Written on: FRM-SBS-07, question 6FRM-SBS-07 Q6

Step 7

Service Manager

Accept the referral in writing and record the engagement date.

Tell the referrer the band, the Practitioner's name and the dates for the risk evaluation and the interim plan. The engagement date is the date we agree in writing to develop the plan, which is the day you accept in writing, or the date a regulated restrictive practice was first used and led to the referral, whichever is earlier (our standard; POL-SBS-07 Ground rule 4). Say in the acceptance that it is the start date for developing the plan for the purposes of the Rules, s 19. Where the first use was before our acceptance, the clocks are already running: tell the Clinical Lead and the Chief Executive the same day if the interim plan due date is less than 5 business days away or has passed. Open the plan row in REG-SBS-01 as an interim plan. Enter the engagement date and both legal due dates, worked out as PRO-BSP-03 sets. Set our own target date for the interim plan from Decision table 3.

Result
Both clocks are running, and the plan row and the target date exist.
Record
FRM-SBS-07 Q7; FRM-SBS-03 Q3 and Q5; REG-SBS-01 (plan number and version; plan type; engaged on; interim plan due; comprehensive plan due)
Time limit
The same business day as the decision at step 5 (our standard)

Carries out: Policy, commitment 2Policy C2Policy, commitment 5Policy C5Written on: FRM-SBS-07, question 7FRM-SBS-07 Q7FRM-SBS-03, question 3FRM-SBS-03 Q3FRM-SBS-03, question 5FRM-SBS-03 Q5

Step 8

Service Manager

If a regulated restrictive practice has been used:

Tell the provider that used the practice the dates that apply to it.

Where the use is likely to continue, that provider has its own limits. It must take all reasonable steps to have an interim plan made within 1 month of the first use. A comprehensive plan is due within 6 months (Rules, s 11(2), s 12(2) and s 13(2)). Those dates can end before ours. Give them in writing with the first use date from FRM-SBS-03. Tell the Clinical Lead if the 1 month date is less than 5 business days away.

Result
The provider knows its own limits, and we know if ours must be faster.
Record
FRM-SBS-07 Q5
Time limit
On the day you accept the referral (our standard)

Carries out: Policy, commitment 5Policy C5Written on: FRM-SBS-07, question 5FRM-SBS-07 Q5

Step 9

Warning. Phone advice to use a restrictive practice, with no plan and no authorisation, can make that use unauthorised. The provider that uses it may then have to report it as a reportable incident.

Practitioner

Check with the lead implementing provider what is keeping people safe today.

Ask what workers do now when the behaviour happens. Ask whether anyone is hurt and whether any restrictive practice is in use. Ask who is on shift tonight. Agree who phones whom if things get worse. Point them to the emergency steps in the participant's support plan (FRM-SUP-02 Participant Support Plan Template). If the participant has no provider yet, do this with the family or carers who support them. Do not tell anyone to use a restrictive practice.

Result
People are as safe as we can make them until the plan is issued, and the provider has our number.
Record
FRM-SBS-07 Q8
Time limit
The same day as the engagement date for danger now, and within 1 business day of it for urgent (our standard)

Carries out: Policy, commitment 3Policy C3Written on: FRM-SBS-07, question 8FRM-SBS-07 Q8

Involve the participant

Step 10

Practitioner

Tell the participant what is happening and how they can take part.

Use their way of communicating (FRM-RGT-01 Communication, Advocacy and Support Preferences Form). Say who we are, who referred them and what we will do. Offer an independent advocate and a support person of their choice. Ask how and when they want to talk.

Result
The participant knows what is happening and has chosen how to take part.
Record
FRM-SBS-03 Q9 and Q14
Time limit
Within 1 business day of the engagement date for danger now, and within 3 for urgent (our standard)

Carries out: Policy, commitment 6Policy C6Written on: FRM-SBS-03, question 9FRM-SBS-03 Q9FRM-SBS-03, question 14FRM-SBS-03 Q14

Step 11

Practitioner

Ask for consent to collect, use and share information for this plan.

Presume the participant can decide, with support (POL-RGT-03 Independence and Informed Choice Policy). Where someone else holds legal authority, see the order or instrument and note what it covers. Ask which family, carers and others we may talk to, and which we may give the plan and to. Write down each person, including every "no". Use FRM-INF-01 Consent to Collect, Use and Share Information Form.

Result
We know who can decide, and who we may talk to and share with.
Record
FRM-SBS-03 Q10 to Q13; REG-SBS-01 (who decides; consent to assess and to collect information; consent)
Time limit
At the first conversation with the participant (our standard)

Carries out: Policy, commitment 6Policy C6Policy, commitment 7Policy C7Policy, commitment 13Policy C13Written on: FRM-SBS-03, question 10FRM-SBS-03 Q10FRM-SBS-03, question 11FRM-SBS-03 Q11FRM-SBS-03, question 12FRM-SBS-03 Q12FRM-SBS-03, question 13FRM-SBS-03 Q13and 1 more

Evaluate the risk

Step 12

Practitioner

Ask the participant how they see the behaviour and the risk.

Ask what happens, what helps, what makes it worse and what worries them. Ask what they want. If they do not use words, watch how they respond and ask the people who know their signs. Let a support person stay. Write their words or signs, not yours. If they choose not to take part, respect that, record why and offer again when you show them the draft.

Result
The participant's view is part of the risk evaluation.
Record
FRM-SBS-07 Q9
Time limit
Within 2 business days of the engagement date for danger now, and within 4 for urgent (our standard)

Carries out: Policy, commitment 6Policy C6Policy, commitment 8Policy C8Written on: FRM-SBS-07, question 9FRM-SBS-07 Q9

Step 13

Practitioner

Hold the risk evaluation with each implementing provider.

Include the manager and a worker who knows the participant well. Ask what the behaviour looks like, when it happens and what workers do. Ask who else is at risk. Ask for their records from the last 3 months: incidents, injuries, restrictive practice use and behaviour data. Note who gave you each record and when. If the participant has no provider yet, hold it with the family or carers who will carry out the plan. Ask the referrer or the support coordinator to find a provider before the plan is issued.

Result
Each implementing provider has taken part and given us what it holds.
Record
FRM-SBS-07 Q10 and Q11; REG-SBS-01 (implementing providers consulted)
Time limit
Within 2 business days of the engagement date for danger now, and within 4 for urgent (our standard)

Carries out: Policy, commitment 7Policy C7Policy, commitment 8Policy C8Written on: FRM-SBS-07, question 10FRM-SBS-07 Q10FRM-SBS-07, question 11FRM-SBS-07 Q11

Step 14

Practitioner

Gather what other people and services already know.

Ask the family, carers or guardian the participant agreed to. Ask the services involved, such as the treating doctor, a mental health service, a hospital, the police, a school or a day service. Read earlier assessments and plans. Note what worked and what did not. Record each source and the date.

Result
The plan builds on what is known and does not repeat a strategy that failed.
Record
FRM-SBS-07 Q12 and Q13; REG-SBS-01 (sources used)
Time limit
Within 2 business days of the engagement date for danger now, and within 4 for urgent (our standard)

Carries out: Policy, commitment 7Policy C7Written on: FRM-SBS-07, question 12FRM-SBS-07 Q12FRM-SBS-07, question 13FRM-SBS-07 Q13

Step 15

Practitioner

Describe the behaviour and what is happening around it.

Say what it looks like, how often it happens, how long it lasts and how strong it is. Say what comes before, during and after it. Say when the risk is lower and when it is higher. Write your working view of why it happens, and mark it as a working view. The full functional behaviour assessment comes with the comprehensive plan.

Result
Everyone reads the same description, and the plan rests on a stated view.
Record
FRM-SBS-07 Q14 and Q15

7If it goes wrong

  • The participant, or the person with legal authority, will not consent. Explain what it means. Offer an independent advocate. Tell the Clinical Supervisor the same day. Go on with the collection and consultation that the Rules require for a plan containing a restrictive practice (Rules, s 20(3)), collect only what the plan needs, and record the refusal and what was collected despite it (POL-SBS-07 Ground rule 8). Keep the safety arrangements from step 9 going. Ask again after 10 business days if they agree (our standard).
  • A provider will not take part, or will not send its records. Write each attempt at Q11. Tell the Clinical Supervisor the same day. Go ahead on what you have, and say in the plan what is missing. If the provider will not follow the plan, tell the Commissioner as PRO-SBS-04 Behaviour Support Plan Monitoring and Review Procedure sets out.
  • The Practitioner is absent or unwell. The Service Manager gives the plan to the cover Practitioner. For danger now that is the same business day, and for urgent within 1 business day. If nobody can start in time, the Service Manager tells the referrer that day and helps them find another specialist behaviour support provider. The engagement date and the due dates do not change.
  • A deadline will be missed. Tell the Clinical Lead and the Chief Executive the same day. Do it at least 7 days before the date where you can. Tell the referrer and each implementing provider in writing, with the new date. Keep the safety arrangements going. Where the limit is set by law, the Chief Executive decides what else must be done. Record the reason on the plan row. Never change a date on the register to hide a late step.
  • The referral shows a restrictive practice used without authorisation, or outside the plan. The provider that used it must treat it as a possible reportable incident. It notifies the Commissioner (Incident Rules, s 16 and s 21). Tell that provider's manager the same day, and start PRO-SBS-05 Reportable Incidents Involving the Use of a Restrictive Practice Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support). Carry on with this procedure. If our own worker used the practice, complete FRM-INC-01 Incident Report Form and follow PRO-INC-01 Incident Management Procedure.
  • You suspect abuse, neglect or exploitation. Tell the Service Manager at once and follow PRO-SGD-01 Violence, Abuse, Neglect, Exploitation and Discrimination Procedure.
  • You are worried about a colleague or a manager. Tell the Clinical Supervisor. If it is about the Clinical Supervisor, tell the Clinical Lead. If it is about the Service Manager or the Clinical Lead, tell the Chief Executive. If it is about the Chief Executive, tell the chair of the governing body, or the independent contact for concerns. For a sole Practitioner's own work, tell the Clinical Supervisor.
  • A provider says it cannot follow the plan. Find out why, with the Clinical Supervisor. Arrange any training under PRO-SBS-03 Supporting the Implementation of the Behaviour Support Plan Procedure. If the plan still cannot be followed, follow PRO-SBS-04 for telling the Commissioner.
  • The participant or family disagrees with the plan. Write their view in their words on the cover sheet. Change what you can and say why where you cannot. Tell them how to complain (POL-FBK-01 Feedback and Complaints Management Policy). If the disagreement is about a restrictive practice, the authorisation process of the state or territory decides whether it may be used, not the Practitioner.
  • Systems are down. Use the paper copies of FRM-SBS-03, FRM-SBS-07 and FRM-BSP-02. The Service Manager enters them within 2 business days of the system coming back (our standard).

8Done means

  • The participant has had their say and holds an interim plan in a form they can use. They know how to ask for a change and how to complain.
  • Each implementing provider took part in the risk evaluation, considered the plan, was coached in it and can carry it out. The support network was given guidance only where the participant agreed.
  • The plan was issued by its due date. Where it contains a regulated restrictive practice, it is lodged and the reference is recorded.
  • FRM-SBS-07 is complete and signed. The plan row in REG-SBS-01 is up to date, with the first check, the monthly check and the date the comprehensive plan is due.
  • The interim plan has ended with a reason, and the participant is not left without a plan they need.

form.intro:
Use this cover sheet and lodgement record for every behaviour support plan we write, interim or comprehensive. It records who wrote the plan and which template it is on. It records who has seen it and who accepted it. It also records whether the plan went to the Commissioner and where it is filed.

This sheet is not the plan, and it is not a form the Commissioner has approved. The plan itself is written on the Commission's current template, our own approved template that holds every item in the Commission's plan checklist, or the template a state or territory authorising body requires (Behaviour Support Rules, section 23(1)). A plan that contains a regulated restrictive practice is lodged by the Practitioner in the Commission's portal with the attachments it requires. Check the Commission's website for the current checklist and template edition on the day you start. This library does not reproduce the Commission's template.

The Practitioner completes sections A to E, except that the answers Q14, and the Practitioner answers Q18 after lodging. The Service Manager answers Q17 and Q19 and prepares the lodgement.

Have ready:

  • the assessment report (FRM-SBS-03 Functional Behaviour Assessment Report Template) and the participant's consent record (FRM-INF-01 Consent to Collect, Use and Share Information Form)
  • the restrictive practice consultation record (FRM-SBS-02 Restrictive Practice Consultation Record), if the plan has a practice
  • the contact details of each implementing provider.

What happens next: the Service Manager copies the answers marked for REG-SBS-01 Behaviour Support Plan Register to the plan row within 2 business days. The sheet is filed with the plan.

"Behaviour Support Rules" here means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Restrictive Practices and Behaviour Support) Rules 2018.
form.privacy:
We collect this information to show that the plan was written, checked, shared and lodged as the law and the participant's wishes require. It names the participant and the providers who carry out their plan.

The Practitioner, the Clinical Supervisor, the Service Manager and the Quality Manager read it. We give the plan to the NDIS Commissioner when it contains a regulated restrictive practice. We share the plan with other people only as the participant, or their decision maker, agreed at Q9.

The participant can see this sheet and ask us to correct it. POL-INF-01 Information Management Policy sets how we store and protect it.
form.after:
1. The Practitioner gives the draft plan and this sheet to the Clinical Supervisor (PRO-BSP-03 step 24). The Clinical Supervisor answers within 5 business days, or 2 business days for an interim plan.
  2. After finalising, the Practitioner gives the Service Manager the finished plan and this sheet the same day (PRO-BSP-03 step 25).
  3. For a plan with a regulated restrictive practice, the Practitioner lodges it within 5 business days of the date at Q15, with the Service Manager preparing the lodgement (PRO-BSP-03 step 27).
  4. The Service Manager updates REG-SBS-01 Behaviour Support Plan Register within 2 business days of each stage (PRO-BSP-03 step 30).
  5. The plan, this sheet and the Commission's confirmation are filed together.
  6. A sole Practitioner does the Service Manager's tasks themselves. Their outside Clinical Supervisor does the check.
