questions.text: What evidence supports each statement, and what would show it wrong?
questions.hint: Name the data. Say how you tested it, for example by changing one thing and watching.

questions.text: Which other explanations did you rule out or treat?
questions.hint: Pain, illness, medicine effects, sleep, hearing, vision, unmet communication, trauma, noise and change.

questions.text: What skill or behaviour could meet the same need more safely?
questions.hint: One line for each behaviour. It must be a skill the participant can learn and use.

questions.section: Section G: Restrictive practices now in use
questions.text: Is any restrictive practice used with the participant now, regulated or not?
questions.hint: One line each: what is done, where, who does it, how often and since when. Write "None" if there is none. Examples: a locked room (seclusion); a medicine given to change behaviour (chemical restraint); a lap belt or bed rail used to stop movement (mechanical restraint); holding a person still (physical restraint); a locked cupboard, fridge or gate that stops access (environmental restraint).

questions.section: Section G: Restrictive practices now in use
questions.text: For each practice, what is its type, its authorisation and its place in a plan?
questions.hint: Type: seclusion, chemical, mechanical, physical, environmental or other. <button type="button" class="term" data-term="authorisation" data-def="the permission a state or territory gives, through its own process, for a regulated restrictive practice. Some states and territories have no such process." data-source="POL-SBS-07">Authorisation</button>: the body, the date and the expiry, or "not needed", or "none". Say whether it is in a current plan and whether that plan was lodged.

questions.section: Section G: Restrictive practices now in use
questions.text: Did you see any practice that could cause serious harm? What did you do, and when?
questions.hint: For example a restraint that restricts breathing. Give the time you called 000 if anyone was in danger, the time you told the person to stop and the time you told the Service Manager. Record it on our incident system as a witnessed event, tell the implementing provider in writing the same day that it must notify the Commission, and start PRO-SBS-05 Reportable Incidents Involving the Use of a Restrictive Practice Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support). The Quality Manager decides whether it is also reportable by us.

questions.section: Section G: Restrictive practices now in use
questions.text: What does the assessment show about reducing or ending each practice?
questions.hint: Say which unmet need or skill would make the practice unnecessary.

questions.section: Section G: Restrictive practices now in use
questions.text: Do you think a regulated restrictive practice may be needed in the plan?
questions.hint: If yes, stop and tell the Service Manager. Start PRO-SBS-02 Restrictive Practices Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support) before the plan is drafted. This report never recommends one.

questions.section: Section H: Other supports and services
questions.text: What other supports and services does the participant use?
questions.hint: One line each: service, what it does, the contact, and what it does when the behaviour happens. Include health, mental health, education, housing, justice, day and community services.

questions.section: Section H: Other supports and services
questions.text: How should these services fit together, and which have agreed to a protocol?
questions.hint: Say what each service and each implementing provider must do, and who tells whom. With the participant's consent, ask each service to agree. Give the date each agreed.

questions.section: Section I: Recommendations for the plan
questions.text: What changes to the environment do you recommend?
questions.hint: Start here: noise, space, light, routine, staff and rules.

questions.section: Section I: Recommendations for the plan
questions.text: What skills should we teach, and what replacement behaviours do you recommend?
questions.hint: Link each to a function in Section F.

questions.section: Section I: Recommendations for the plan
questions.text: What proactive strategies do you recommend?
questions.hint: Think about daily life, communication, routines, relationships, activities and choice.

questions.section: Section I: Recommendations for the plan
questions.text: What response strategies do you recommend for when the behaviour happens?
questions.hint: Strategies that keep people safe and help the participant settle. Never a restrictive practice.

questions.section: Section I: Recommendations for the plan
questions.text: What evidence supports each recommended strategy?
questions.hint: One line for each strategy: the function it answers, the assessment data it rests on, and the practice <button type="button" class="term" data-term="guidance" data-def="teaching and coaching on how to carry out the plan, with a check that it was understood." data-source="POL-SBS-07">guidance</button> or research behind it, such as the Commission's behaviour support guidance or a recognised positive behaviour support framework. Never include a strategy that does not answer a function.

questions.section: Section I: Recommendations for the plan
questions.text: What data should each implementing provider collect, how often, and how will we check the plan is followed?
questions.hint: Name the form, the measure and the day each month it reaches us.

questions.section: Section I: Recommendations for the plan
questions.text: What training do the implementing providers need?
questions.hint: Name the topic and who needs it. PRO-SBS-03 Supporting the Implementation of the Behaviour Support Plan Procedure arranges it.

questions.section: Section I: Recommendations for the plan
questions.text: How can the participant take part in community activities and learn new skills that reduce any need for a restrictive practice?
questions.hint: Give at least one activity or skill.

questions.section: Section J: Sharing, tools and review
questions.text: When and how did you go through the findings with the participant, and what did they say?
questions.hint: Give the date, the format, who helped, their response and any disagreement in their words.

questions.section: Section J: Sharing, tools and review
questions.text: Which implementing providers were consulted and given the findings, and what did each say?
questions.hint: Only with the participant's consent. One line each: provider, date and what they said.

questions.section: Section J: Sharing, tools and review
questions.text: Was an automated or AI tool used for any part of this report?
questions.hint: If yes, name the tool, say what it was used for and what information went in. Nothing that identifies the participant may go into a tool that POL-TEC-01 Artificial Intelligence and Automated Tools Policy has not approved.

questions.section: Section J: Sharing, tools and review
questions.text: When will we look at this assessment again, and what would make us look sooner?
questions.hint: No more than 12 months after the report is finalised. Sooner for a new setting, a health change, a loss or a new restrictive practice.

questions.section: Section J: Sharing, tools and review
questions.text: Did the Clinical Supervisor check this report? Give the date and the outcome.
questions.hint: The <button type="button" class="term" data-term="Clinical Supervisor" data-def="an experienced Practitioner who checks the Practitioner's work and supports their practice." data-source="POL-SBS-07">Clinical Supervisor</button> answers. The outcome is accepted, or returned with the changes needed.

form.intro:
Use this template to write the assessment report. It shows what we found out about the participant and why, and what we recommend for their plan.

The Practitioner completes Sections B to J, and nobody else signs the clinical content. Section A is completed by the Service Manager from the plan row in REG-SBS-01 (PRO-BSP-03 steps 1 to 5), and the Practitioner copies the plan number into the report. Workers, family members and managers give information and records. They do not write findings. Only a specialist behaviour support provider uses this template. An implementing provider does not write assessment reports; it supplies behaviour records (FRM-BSP-04 Behaviour Record) to the Practitioner.

Start the report on the day the referral is logged. Fill it in as the assessment goes. Finalise it within 49 days of the engagement date (our standard).

Have ready:

  • the referral and the service agreement
  • the participant's communication preferences (FRM-RGT-01 Communication, Advocacy and Support Preferences Form) and their consent record (FRM-INF-01 Consent to Collect, Use and Share Information Form)
  • earlier plans and assessments, and the data from each implementing provider.

What happens next: the Clinical Supervisor checks the report within 3 . The Practitioner goes through it with the participant within 5 business days of the check. The Service Manager copies the answers marked for REG-SBS-01 Behaviour Support Plan Register to the plan row within 2 business days.

"Behaviour Support Rules" here means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Restrictive Practices and Behaviour Support) Rules 2018.
form.privacy:
We collect this information to understand the participant and why they behave as they do, so we can write a plan that helps them. It holds sensitive information about their health, history and behaviour.

The Practitioner, the Clinical Supervisor and the Service Manager read it. We ask for information only from the people and services the participant agreed to (Q12), except that the law requires us to consult the providers who may use a restrictive practice; we tell the participant first and share only what they need. We share the report only with the people they agreed to (Q13). We give a plan with a regulated restrictive practice, and this report with it, to the NDIS Commissioner, as the Behaviour Support Rules require.

The participant can see this report and ask us to correct it. They can ask us to stop at any time. FRM-INF-02 Request to Access or Correct Personal Information Form is the form to ask. POL-INF-01 Information Management Policy sets how we store and protect it.
form.after:
1. The Practitioner gives the finished report to the Clinical Supervisor the same day (PRO-BSP-03 step 15).
  2. The Clinical Supervisor checks it within 3 business days and signs the sign-off block (PRO-BSP-03 step 16).
  3. The Practitioner goes through it with the participant within 5 business days of the check (PRO-BSP-03 step 17).
  4. The Service Manager copies each answer marked for REG-SBS-01 Behaviour Support Plan Register to the plan row within 2 business days (PRO-BSP-03 step 30).
  5. The report is filed on the participant's file. We share it only as Q13 says.
  6. A sole Practitioner files the report and updates the register themselves. The outside Clinical Supervisor does the check.

form.intro:
Use this record for every . It shows how we decided the plan. It records the urgency, who we talked to, the risks, what we agreed and what we did to put the plan to work. The plan itself is written on the Commissioner's approved form (FRM-BSP-02 Behaviour Support Plan Cover Sheet and Lodgement Record). This record does not replace it.

This record authorises no restrictive practice. Only the authorisation process of the state or territory can do that.

Only a specialist behaviour support provider uses this record. A provider that only implements plans uses FRM-BSP-08 Interim Behaviour Support Engagement Record.

This record holds only what is new in an interim plan. The referral, the engagement date, the and the consent are on FRM-SBS-03 Functional Behaviour Assessment Report Template. The cover sheet FRM-BSP-02 holds the plan's checks, acceptance and lodgement. FRM-SBS-04 Behaviour Support Plan Handover and Training Record holds the handover. FRM-SBS-05 Behaviour Support Plan Review Record holds the monthly checks. Do not write the same answer twice.

Who completes it:

  • Section A: whoever takes the referral starts it. The and the Service Manager finish it.
  • Sections B to G: the Practitioner, as each step of PRO-SBS-06 Interim Behaviour Support Plans Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support) is done.
  • Q30: the Practitioner records it, and the Service Manager closes the record.

Answer the questions in section D only when the answer to Q4 shows a practice. Each question in section D is answered once for each practice.

Have ready: the referral and any earlier plans. Have the participant's communication preferences (FRM-RGT-01 Communication, Advocacy and Support Preferences Form). Have their consent record (FRM-INF-01 Consent to Collect, Use and Share Information Form). Have the authorisation schedule in REG-QMS-03 Compliance Obligations Register.

Three answers open the next step. A band of "Not immediate" or "Covered by a current plan" at Q2 sends the referral to another pathway. A practice at Q4 opens section D and the lodgement duty. A band of "Danger now" opens the 000 call at Q3.

What happens next: the Service Manager copies the answers marked for REG-SBS-01 Behaviour Support Plan Register to the plan row. This is within 2 business days of the stage, as the register's entry rules set. PRO-SBS-06 sets every step.

When systems are down, use the paper copy. Enter it in the system within 2 business days of the system coming back (our standard).
form.privacy:
We collect this information to work out how to keep a participant and other people safe. We use it to write an interim plan and to help those who carry it out. Some of it is health information, which is sensitive.

The Practitioner, the Clinical Supervisor and the Service Manager read this record. We give the providers who carry out the plan the parts they need. We share with a participant's only what the participant agreed to. We a plan that contains a regulated restrictive practice with the NDIS Commissioner, because the law requires it.

If you are the participant, you can ask to see this record and ask us to correct it. You can have an advocate with you. You can tell us you disagree, and we will write it down in your words. To complain, use POL-FBK-01 Feedback and Complaints Management Policy. POL-INF-01 Information Management Policy sets how we store this record and how long we keep it.
form.after:
1. The Practitioner files this record on the participant's file the day it is started, and keeps it up to date as each step is done.
  2. The Service Manager copies each answer marked for REG-SBS-01 to the plan row within 2 business days of the stage (our standard).
  3. The Clinical Supervisor reads this record with the draft plan, and signs the check on the cover sheet, within 2 business days of the providers' replies and inside the plan's issue date.
  4. The Service Manager reads this record every week while the plan is open, using step 37 of PRO-SBS-06. The Quality Manager reads every open record once a month.
  5. A sole Practitioner files the record and updates the plan row themselves. The external Clinical Supervisor does the check.

register.proves:
This register is the one running record of every behaviour support plan [Provider name] writes. It has three sheets. On the plan sheet each row is one plan version. It shows when we were engaged and who wrote the plan. It shows what the participant agreed to and which accepted the plan. It shows whether the plan reached the Commissioner on time and when it is next due for review. On the practice sheet each row is one in one plan, keyed on the plan number in col A, and holds the answers FRM-SBS-02 Restrictive Practice Consultation Record routes here, with every status the practice has held. On the incident review sheet each row is one review under FRM-SBS-06 Restrictive Practice Incident Review Record of an emergency or unauthorised use, keyed on the plan number in col A.

"Behaviour Support Rules" here means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Restrictive Practices and Behaviour Support) Rules 2018.

  • Indicators evidenced: s 40 (1) to s 40 (6). The register also holds the plan dates and records that s 39, s 41, s 42, s 43 and s 44 rely on. Those threads write to the columns marked with their indicators.
  • Legal basis: the Behaviour Support Rules. Sections 17 and 18 say who writes. Section 19 sets time limits. Section 20 says how plans are developed and section 21 what they contain. Sections 22 to 24 cover review, form and lodgement.
  • Retention: keep each row for 7 years from the day the plan is superseded or ends (our standard). We set it to match the 7 years in section 15(3) of the Behaviour Support Rules for records of the use of a regulated restrictive practice.
  • Other law can require longer, for example for records about a child. For a participant under 18, keep the row until they turn 25 or for 7 years, whichever is later (our standard pending state law). Check REG-INF-02 Records Retention and Disposal Register and the law of [state or territory] before any row is destroyed.

Columns H and I are worked out and never typed over. Columns AB, AC, AD and AW are filled only when col Z lists a regulated restrictive practice, and summarise the practice sheet. Columns AN to AP are filled only when col AM is yes. Columns AR to BA are filled from the forms named in the Filled from column. The practice sheet columns RP-A to RP-R are filled from FRM-SBS-02, one row per practice per plan. The incident review sheet columns IR-A to IR-O are filled from FRM-SBS-06, one row per review; col AZ summarises them.
register.entry:
1. The Service Manager opens the row and keeps it. A sole does both. Open the row on the day we confirm the referral (our standard).
  2. Use one row for each plan version. A new version is a new row. Link it to the one it replaces in col D and col BD.
  3. The Practitioner gives each answer to the Service Manager within 1 of recording it on the form. The forms are FRM-SBS-03 Functional Behaviour Assessment Report Template and FRM-BSP-02 Behaviour Support Plan Cover Sheet and Lodgement Record for the plan sheet, and FRM-SBS-02 Restrictive Practice Consultation Record for the practice sheet. The Service Manager enters it within 2 business days of the stage (our standard).
  4. Columns that hold a list (col R, col Z, col AC, col AD, col AG, col AK, col AW and col BB, and practice sheet cols RP-P and RP-R) take a new dated line for each change. Never overwrite a line. An authorisation status is never typed over: every status the practice has held stays visible with its date.
  5. Never overwrite or delete an entry. A correction is a new version of the row, with the date, your name and the reason.
  6. Never type over a worked-out date. To change the in col F, record the reason and the name of the who agreed.
  7. When systems are down, use the paper forms. The Service Manager enters them within 2 business days of the system coming back.
  8. When a row is about the work of the Service Manager or the Practitioner who keeps it, the Chief Executive holds it. When it is about the Chief Executive, the holds it. In a sole practitioner provider the Practitioner keeps every row, and the outside Clinical Supervisor reviews them every month under How we review.
  9. The practice sheet is the second sheet of this register: one row per regulated restrictive practice per plan, keyed on the plan number in col A, with cols RP-A to RP-R. Open a practice row when col Z first lists or proposes the practice. The incident review sheet is the third sheet: one row per FRM-SBS-06 review, keyed on col A, with cols IR-A to IR-O; open a row when a review starts and summarise it in col AZ. A small provider can keep the other list columns on a further sheet in the same way; each line carries the plan number from col A.

A row is closed only when all of these are true:

  • the plan has been replaced by a later version that is in force, or the plan has ended, or the participant has left us, and col BD says which
  • every lodgement is done and recorded in col AO
  • every open line in col BB is done, or has moved to REG-QMS-01 Continuous Improvement Register with an owner and a due date
  • the Service Manager has checked the row and recorded the closing date.

register.rows: The rows are the data. They are kept in the workbook or system built to this specification, not in this document. The register has three sheets: the plan sheet (one row per plan version, cols A to BF), the practice sheet (one row per regulated restrictive practice per plan, cols RP-A to RP-R, keyed on col A) and the incident review sheet (one row per FRM-SBS-06 review, cols IR-A to IR-O, keyed on col A). Where a plan sheet cell would otherwise hold a list of practices or reviews, the second or third sheet holds the detail and the plan sheet cell summarises it. Every column name on the plan sheet is kept stable, because other documents cite the columns by name.
